chat.dxr_mc.pix_capture.fail.missing: this MCDR.dll has no capture entry point - rebuild the native library.
chat.dxr_mc.pix_capture.fail.recording: PIX is already recording; press the key again once it has stopped.

dxr_mc.configuration.debug.asyncRenderTh: Run the dedicated render thread (acquire / present / fence waits off the main thread). OFF is a diagnostic that isolates the render thread from the recording thread.
dxr_mc.configuration.debug.debugLayer.to: Create the device with the Direct3D 12 debug layer installed. Much slower; useful when the log reports a broken command.
dxr_mc.configuration.debug.dumpHlsl.tool: Write every translated HLSL pair into dxrmc/hlsl/. This is how you see what the SPIR-V cross-compiler actually emitted.
dxr_mc.configuration.debug.failDevice.to: Make backend creation fail on purpose to verify the no-fallback crash path. Development check; always leave OFF.
dxr_mc.configuration.debug.meshDiagnosti: One-shot isolation test for texture write versus read-back: CLEAR clears the target through a mesh dispatch and reads it back, PASS runs the full mesh pass and reads it back. Development check; keep NONE on a normal start.
Do not show the blocking native message box when the backend fails (automated runs would hang on it). Always leave OFF when playing.
dxr_mc.configuration.debug.pixCapture.to: Load Microsoft PIX's GPU capture layer (WinPixGpuCapturer.dll) at startup so PIX can capture this process. The layer has to be loaded before the first Direct3D 12 device is created, so changing this requires a game restart. PIX must be running to save a capture.
dxr_mc.configuration.debug.pixCaptureFra: PIX Capture Frames per Key Press

How many frames one key-press capture records, read when the key is pressed. 600 frames is about ten seconds at 60 fps, which is already a large file - a capture with the memory events on runs to hundreds of megabytes.
Where PIX lives: its install directory (holding WinPixGpuCapturer.dll, WinPixTimingCapturer.dll and WinPixEventRuntime_OneCore.dll) or one of those DLLs. Leave it empty for a normal install - the default Program Files locations are searched.
dxr_mc.configuration.debug.pixTimingCapt: Arm the PIX capture key (Options - Controls - DXRMC, default F9). Press it in game and PIX starts recording into run/pix/dxrmc-capture-N.wpix; press it again to stop early, or let it end after pixCaptureFrames frames. Every press writes a new file and the frame budget is read at the moment of the press, so no restart is needed. PIX's own counters recording stays inside the PIX session until saved, and the timing capture PIX starts itself writes to %TEMP% under a name PIX picks; only PIXBeginCapture, called from inside the process, writes where we ask. A timing capture records through ETW sessions, and creating those needs an elevated (administrator) token: on this machine being in the built-in Performance Log Users group was measured not to be enough (2026-10-21), and an elevated terminal is not enough on its own either because gradlew reuses a daemon started without elevation - run gradlew --stop first.
dxr_mc.configuration.debug.profiling.too: Print the CPU/GPU frame-time instrumentation every second. Off by default.
dxr_mc.configuration.debug.selfTestCompu: Compile a compute shader (cs_6_8), create a compute pipeline, dispatch it into a storage texture and read it back once at startup. Proves the compute path that the shading-rate image (P235) builds on; development check, keep OFF on a normal start.
Compile an HLSL mesh shader, dispatch it and read the target back once at startup. Development check; keep OFF on a normal start.
dxr_mc.configuration.debug.selfTestSurfa: Run the swapchain self-test on the real window at startup. Development check; it binds a second Present swapchain, so leave it OFF.
dxr_mc.configuration.debug.skipGlSwap.to: Make the GL surface present() a no-op. OFF by default: with the normal no-API window there is no GL context to present from anyway. Turn it ON only when a real GL context exists (see renderer glContext) and its swapping steals the OSD.
dxr_mc.configuration.debug.temporalChain: Force the experimental temporal chain on (jitter, projection injection, velocity attachment) even when neither TAA nor DLAA / DLSS is selected. Also gates the standalone velocity pass. Development switch; leave OFF unless a test needs it.
dxr_mc.configuration.debug.temporalJitte: Inject the sub-pixel jitter into the level projection. ON by default; turning it OFF keeps the rest of the temporal chain alive and is used to tell a jitter problem from a matrix-capture problem.
dxr_mc.configuration.debug.tooltip: Diagnostics that have to be decided before the renderer starts. Read once, when the config loads.
dxr_mc.configuration.dlss.frameGeneratio: DLSS frame generation. OFF disables it, ON generates the fixed number of extra frames below, DYNAMIC lets the driver pick the count to match the display (driver 595.41+). Needs Reflex enabled; requires the sl.dlss_g runtime in the game directory.
Extra frames generated per rendered frame when Frame Generation is ON (1-5): n frames means (n+1)x output, up to 6x. Higher means more latency.
dxr_mc.configuration.dlss.implementation: NGX (default) runs DLSS in-process; STREAMLINE uses the newer sl.dlss layer. Switching needs a game restart.
dxr_mc.configuration.dlss.outputHandover: ON (default) hands a JVM-created UAV texture to native as the DLSS output target - the shipped path. OFF makes native use its own private texture instead, which cannot be written on some machines (troubleshooting only).
dxr_mc.configuration.dlss.reflexFrameLim: Reflex limits the frame rate itself, in microseconds per frame (0 = off, 144 fps = 6944). It stays accurate even when the CPU is far ahead of the GPU.
dxr_mc.configuration.dlss.tooltip: Which upscaler backend the native DLL drives.
dxr_mc.configuration.logging.logLevel.to: Level for everything this mod prints - the renderer and the native DLL alike.
dxr_mc.configuration.logging.nativeLogFi: Absolute path for a copy of the native log. Empty (default) keeps it in the normal game log only.
dxr_mc.configuration.logging.nativeVerbo: Force the native DLL to DEBUG regardless of the log level above. Kept separate because the DLL is by far the loudest writer, and raising only it (without turning the renderer logs back on) is the common case.
dxr_mc.configuration.logging.shutdownTra: Keep the native shutdown trace (the destroySurface/destroyDevice stage lines) visible at any log level. They are INFO lines, not errors - they used to be logged as ERROR, so every normal exit spammed the console. ON: they always show up, which is the only trail if quitting hangs. OFF: they become ordinary INFO lines and the default ERROR level hides them.
dxr_mc.configuration.logging.tooltip: What this mod prints, and where. ERROR (the default) keeps the console usable: only errors are printed. WARN adds warnings, INFO adds per-load diagnostics, DEBUG/TRACE add the high-frequency dumps (shader sources, pipeline dumps, per-frame tracing). DX12_LOG_VERBOSE=1 still forces DEBUG for one run.
dxr_mc.configuration.mesh.terrain.toolti: Rasterize terrain with mesh shaders. Needs a 12_2 device with mesh shader tier 1. Turning it off leaves terrain undrawn; it is only useful for isolating a mesh regression.
dxr_mc.configuration.mesh.terrain_cull: Cull terrain meshlets with an amplification shader
dxr_mc.configuration.mesh.tooltip: The terrain mesh-shader path (the only terrain rasterization path; no IMR fallback).
dxr_mc.configuration.renderer.allowTeari: ON (default) lets the swapchain use ALLOW_TEARING, which is what low-latency/VRR presentation wants. OFF keeps the chain in DWM composed flip - the mode overlay tools such as RTSS / MSI Afterburner draw their OSD in. Takes effect on the next swapchain creation.
dxr_mc.configuration.renderer.asyncComma: Record multi-draw batches on the worker pool instead of the calling thread. Turning it OFF falls back to serial recording.
dxr_mc.configuration.renderer.asyncWorke: Worker threads used for parallel command recording (1-8). The default of 8 partitions the per-frame segment evenly.
dxr_mc.configuration.renderer.commandBun: How one multi-draw batch is split. AUTO (default) inlines a single bundle for small batches and records in parallel for large ones; SERIAL always uses one bundle (most compatible); PARALLEL always splits across the worker pool.
dxr_mc.configuration.renderer.glContext: Keep a real OpenGL context (restart required)
OFF (default) creates the window without an OpenGL context, which is what makes RTSS / MSI Afterburner draw its OSD through Direct3D 12 and stay visible. Turn it ON only if a feature or another mod needs a live GL context - the DXRMC renderer itself never draws through GL.
dxr_mc.configuration.renderer.presentChi: OFF (default) creates the swapchain on the SDL top-level window, which exclusive fullscreen needs. ON restores the older presentation-child window: always composed flip. Takes effect on the next swapchain creation.
dxr_mc.configuration.renderer.sharpenAmo: Post-sharpen strength (0-1) applied after DLAA / DLSS upscaling. 0 disables it and falls back to a plain blit.
dxr_mc.configuration.renderer.taaSharpen: Post-sharpen strength (0-1) applied after the TAA resolve. TAA is softer than DLAA, so it normally wants a higher value than dlss sharpen.
dxr_mc.configuration.renderer.tooltip: How the Direct3D 12 renderer runs. Read once when the renderer starts, so a change asks for a game restart.
dxr_mc.configuration.section.dxr.mc.clie: Illusion(DXRMC) client settings: renderer, DLSS and diagnostics.
dxr_mc.configuration.title: Illusion Configs
dxr_mc.configuration.vrs.sri.tooltip: Build a screen-space shading rate image every frame from the previous frame's depth (and motion vectors when available), so tiles only get coarsened where the geometry is flat. This is what keeps the horizon from flickering; with it off only the distance bands above decide. Takes effect on the next frame, no restart.
dxr_mc.configuration.vrs.sriEdgePermille: Depth contrast across a tile that keeps it at 1x1. Lower values treat more tiles as edges: safer, less saving. 1000 disables the test.
dxr_mc.configuration.vrs.sriMotionPixels: Screen-space motion above which a tile stays at 1x1. Only used when the velocity pass runs (SMAA, TAA or DLSS).
dxr_mc.configuration.vrs.sriTemporalClam: Never let a tile get coarser than the previous frame's shading rate image. Stops edges from breathing under a still camera; a tile that gets finer stays fine for one extra frame. Takes effect on the next frame, no restart.
dxr_mc.configuration.vrs.terrain_far_blo: Distance in blocks where the farthest shading-rate band starts. About half the view distance keeps the 2X2 edge off the horizon line, where it is easiest to notice.
dxr_mc.configuration.vrs.terrain_near_bl: Terrain closer than this many blocks keeps full 1X1 shading. Lower values move the coarser band towards the camera and save more, at the risk of the band edge landing on what the player is looking at.
dxr_mc.video.lock.aa_dlss: DLSS upscaling already handles temporal resolve; adding TAA/SMAA would double-process
dxr_mc.video.lock.dlss_dlaa: Anti-aliasing is set to DLAA, which owns the DLSS toggle and preset
dxr_mc.video.lock.dlss_framegen: DLSS cannot be turned off while frame generation is on: generated frames are interpolated from the DLSS output
dxr_mc.video.lock.improved_transparency: Locked on: the mesh pipeline has no immediate-mode transparency fallback, so translucent blocks are only composited correctly through OIT (improved transparency).
dxr_mc.video.lock.renderscale_dlss: Render scale is driven by the DLSS preset while upscaling is on
dxr_mc.video.lock.sr_exclusive: the other vendor's upscaler is selected: only one can run at a time
dxr_mc.video.lock.sr_framegen: frame generation interpolates the DLSS output, so DLSS has to stay the upscaler
dxr_mc.video.lock.sr_not_active: Only takes effect while this upscaler is active
dxr_mc.video.lock.sr_other_backend: The upscaler is set to AMD FidelityFX or Intel XeSS below
dxr_mc.video.sr.framegen_absent: Frame generation: not available for this backend yet (v1 only has DLSS-G).
dxr_mc.video.sr.noabi: %s: the native library has no super-resolution entry points (ABI too old)
dxr_mc.video.fg.off: Frame generation is off (no vendor selected)
dxr_mc.video.fg.noabi: Frame generation: the native library has no frame-generation entry points (ABI too old)
dxr_mc.video.fg.rolled_back: Frame generation was switched off automatically (reason: %s). Turn it back on after fixing the cause.
dxr_mc.video.title: Video Settings
options.antiAliasing.tooltip: Anti-aliasing applied by DXRMC's Direct3D 12 backend.
options.dlss.preset.tooltip:
Which generation of neural network DLSS runs (NGX's render preset).

Default: let DLSS pick per quality level.
J: same generation as K, slightly less ghosting but more flicker.
K: NVIDIA's recommended best-image-quality model.
L / M: the stock defaults for Ultra Performance / Performance.

Switching rebuilds the DLSS feature once (the picture is re-created for a frame). If the model's noise flicker bothers you, try the other entries; whole-surface colour flashing on materials is not a model problem and will not improve.
options.dlss.quality.tooltip: Which DLSS performance/quality level to use. Performance renders at the lowest internal resolution and upscales the most (fastest); Quality renders at the highest internal resolution (sharpest). Balanced sits in between. The level applies while DLSS is on; the slider next to it still picks the actual render resolution, so the two together decide the final cost.
options.dlss.tooltip:
Requires an NVIDIA RTX GPU and a matching driver. When on, the world layer is upscaled to the window size by DLSS; the button is greyed out when DLSS is unavailable on this machine.

Render Scale must not be 100%: DLSS needs the world layer and the presented target to be two different textures.
options.frameGeneration.dlssg.tooltip: Interpolates frames with NVIDIA DLSS-G. Requires Reflex and sl.dlss_g in the dxrmc folder.
options.frameGeneration.xessfg.tooltip: Interpolates frames with Intel XeSS-FG. Requires libxess_fg.dll and libxell.dll in dxrmc.
options.frameGeneration.fsrfg.tooltip: Interpolates frames with AMD FidelityFX frame generation. Requires amd_fidelityfx_framegeneration_dx12.dll in dxrmc.
options.frameGeneration.frames.tooltip: Multiplier. The lowest step is Auto: the driver picks the frame count to match the display. Above that, n = (n+1)x output, 6x is the cap.
options.frameGeneration.tooltip: Interpolates extra frames with DLSS-G. Requires DLSS; turning it on also forces NVIDIA Reflex on (while Frame Generation is active it still switches between On and On+Boost, but cannot be turned Off).
options.graphicsApi.tooltip.d3d12: Experimental. Renders through DXRMC's Direct3D 12 backend instead of OpenGL or Vulkan. May reduce performance or cause instability on some systems.
options.hdr.tooltip:
Presents the frame through a scRGB (16-bit float) swap chain instead of SDR, so the display can show the full brightness range.

Auto follows the Windows advanced-colour setting; On forces HDR even on an SDR display (the picture will look overexposed - it is a pipeline test); Off forces SDR.

The setting applies the next time the swap chain is created, which in normal play means after restarting the game.
options.inactivityFpsLimit.never.tooltip: Never lower the framerate while AFK or minimized.
options.reflex.tooltip:
NVIDIA Reflex low-latency mode through Streamline. Off disables it; On keeps the CPU from running ahead of the GPU; On + Boost additionally keeps the GPU clocks high. Requires the Streamline runtime (sl.reflex); greyed out when it is unavailable.

Reflex never changes image quality - it only trades a little CPU headroom for lower input latency.
options.renderScale.tooltip:
P105: the size of the main render target's textures as a percentage of the window - the render resolution, decoupled from the display resolution. 100 is the exact behaviour of the build without this feature. Below 100 the world is shaded at fewer pixels and the final blit stretches the result to the window; above 100 renders more pixels and shrinks them down, the supersampling direction. Cost scales with the pixel count, so 200 is four times the shading of 100. The GUI keeps a window-sized target of its own (P106), so the layout stays correct at any value.

While DLSS is off the slider runs 25-400 in 25% steps (default 100). While DLSS is on it runs 50-90 in 10% steps (default 70), and the two modes remember their own value separately. No restart needed.
options.shadingRate.tooltip: Automatic variable-rate shading (tier 2 groundwork). OFF (the default) issues no RSSetShadingRate at all and leaves the device at 1x1 - the exact behaviour of the build before VRS. AUTO lets the renderer decide per draw and per primitive: solid terrain is coarsened (at most 2x2) while gui, text, sky, particles and cutout/translucent geometry stay 1x1. A device reporting VRS tier 0 refuses the request (the log says so) and stays at 1x1. No restart needed.
options.sr.fsr.quality.tooltip: Selects the render scale for AMD FidelityFX. "Native AA" keeps 100% and lets FSR run without upscaling.
options.sr.fsr.tooltip:
AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution: the world layer is rendered below the window size and rebuilt by AMD's upscaler - the same job DLSS does on NVIDIA cards. Needs the FidelityFX runtime next to MCDR.dll; the row is greyed out when it is missing.

Render Scale must stay below 100%: the upscaler needs a smaller input and a window-sized output. While DLSS upscaling is on, Render Scale follows the DLSS preset, so FSR simply reuses that resolution. FSR and XeSS are mutually exclusive, and frame generation keeps DLSS as the upscaler because it interpolates the DLSS output.
options.sr.mask.tooltip: Feeds the opaque/translucent boundary to the upscaler as a reactive mask (FSR) or responsive mask (XeSS). Off by default: none of the three SDKs needs it.
options.sr.sharpness.tooltip: How much extra sharpening the FSR / XeSS pass applies after reconstruction, 0-100%. 0 leaves the upscaler's own output untouched. DLSS sharpens on its own and ignores this.
options.sr.xess.quality.tooltip: Selects the render scale for Intel XeSS. "Native AA" keeps 100% and lets XeSS run without upscaling.
options.sr.xess.tooltip:
Intel XeSS: the same idea as FSR, rebuilt by Intel's upscaler. XeSS is told the actual render resolution every frame, so any Render Scale below 100% works. Needs libxess.dll next to MCDR.dll; the row is greyed out otherwise.

Mutually exclusive with FSR; frame generation keeps DLSS as the upscaler.
dxr_mc.video.lock.sr_mask_unsupported: Only AMD FidelityFX and Intel XeSS take a reactive / responsive mask
dxr_mc.video.lock.fg_unavailable: Frame generation cannot run on this combination - see the status line above for the reason
dxr_mc.video.sr.latency_absent: Low latency: only NVIDIA Reflex (DLSS) in v1.
